tasks.prompt: Suppose branch A rewords one AI comment's text, and branch B leaves that comment's text alone but its recording updated where the comment goes (the code moved, so the entry's placement metadata changed). When one branch is merged into the other, what does that comment's entry in the merged sidecar hold: whose text, and whose placement? Which code decides it and how does git get there? And what happens instead if both branches had reworded the text differently? Answer from the code; do not change any files.
tasks.answer: The entry takes A's reworded text together with A's whole metadata, including A's unchanged (base) placement, so B's placement update is dropped: in mergeEntry (packages/core/src/merge.ts) a body changed on only one side wins with that side's entry copied whole, because provenance and placement travel with the body they were written with. Git reaches this because `init` marks `.agents/comments/**` with `merge=cairn` and sets `merge.cairn.driver` to `cairn merge-sidecar %O %A %B`, whose runMergeSidecar calls mergeSidecars and writes the result over %A. Metadata is merged per key (placement keys as one unit) only when both bodies are equal. If both sides reworded the text differently, the body is written with `<<<<<<< ours` / `=======` / `>>>>>>> theirs` markers, the id is reported on stderr, and the driver exits 1 so git reports a conflict on that sidecar.

tasks.prompt: When my command calls `click.echo(click.style('hi', fg='red'))`, the color codes show up in a terminal but disappear when I redirect output to a file, and they are also missing from `CliRunner().invoke(...).output` in my tests. How does Click decide whether to strip the ANSI codes, in what order does it consider its inputs, and why does CliRunner output come out plain by default (and how do I keep the codes there)? Point to the functions involved; do not change any files.
answerKey: isatty|not a tty|isn'?t a tty|not a terminal|isn'?t a terminal|non-?terminal|non-?tty|interactive terminal
tasks.answer: `echo` (utils.py) strips when `should_strip_ansi(file, resolve_color_default(color))` returns true. An explicit `color=` passed to echo wins; otherwise resolve_color_default falls back to the current Context's `color` (set via `Context(color=...)`/`invoke(color=...)`, inherited from the parent context); if that is still None, `_compat.should_strip_ansi` strips when the stream is not a TTY (`isatty`) and is not Jupyter kernel output, and leaves streams with a `color` attribute (the progress bar's wrapper) alone. CliRunner.isolation replaces `utils.should_strip_ansi` and `_compat.should_strip_ansi` with a version that, when no color is given, returns `not default_color`, where default_color is the `color` argument of `invoke`/`isolation`, which defaults to False, so output is stripped unless you call `runner.invoke(cli, color=True)`.
